doc: Bluesky / ATProto content, read-only: one message, a conversation, an account. Renders from plain ATProto-shaped data — no network, no clock, no capabilities.

components.name: Post
components.doc: One bluesky message: who wrote it, what it says (with its facets resolved), what it carries and how it was received. Also the row a Thread and a Profile are made of.

messageDocs.name: toggleLike
messageDocs.doc: Like this message, or take the like back. Optimistic: the count moves here and a `liked` / `unliked` bubble says so.

messageDocs.name: toggleRepost
messageDocs.doc: Repost this message, or take the repost back.

messageDocs.name: toggleFold
messageDocs.doc: Fold the replies under this message away, or bring them back. Only a row inside a thread has any.

messageDocs.name: liked
messageDocs.doc: This reader liked the message; carries its uri.

messageDocs.name: unliked
messageDocs.doc: This reader took a like back; carries its uri.

messageDocs.name: reposted
messageDocs.doc: This reader reposted the message; carries its uri.

messageDocs.name: unreposted
messageDocs.doc: This reader took a repost back; carries its uri.

messageDocs.name: summary
messageDocs.doc: The author and the three counts, as one sentence.

messageDocs.name: folded
messageDocs.doc: This row folded its replies away; carries its uri. The row keeps the flag; the thread above is what knows which messages stop rendering because of it.

messageDocs.name: unfolded
messageDocs.doc: This row brought its replies back; carries its uri.

messageDocs.name: foldTitle
messageDocs.doc: What the fold button will do, spelled out — its label is a glyph.

messageDocs.name: owned
messageDocs.doc: Set by whoever builds a row; it draws smaller and sits inside their list.

fields.name: uri
fields.doc: The record's at:// uri (at://<did>/app.bsky.feed.post/<rkey>), which the permalink is derived from.

fields.name: displayName
fields.doc: The author's display name; the handle stands in when it is empty.

fields.name: handle
fields.doc: The author's handle, without the leading @.

fields.name: text
fields.doc: What the message says.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.doc: When it was written, as an ISO 8601 stamp.

fields.name: facets
fields.doc: Rich-text ranges: { byteStart, byteEnd, kind: link|mention|tag, value }. The offsets are UTF-8 byte offsets, as on the wire.

fields.name: images
fields.doc: Attached images as { alt }. Only the alt text is rendered — an untrusted bundle may not name an image source.

fields.name: replyCount
fields.doc: How many replies the record came with.

fields.name: repostCount
fields.doc: How many reposts the record came with.

fields.name: likeCount
fields.doc: How many likes the record came with.

fields.name: liked
fields.doc: Whether this reader has liked it, counted on top of likeCount.

fields.name: reposted
fields.doc: Whether this reader has reposted it, counted on top of repostCount.

fields.name: depth
fields.doc: How deep in a reply tree this message sits; 0 stands on its own. Drawn as that many rails, since an untrusted view has no style attribute to indent with.

fields.name: focus
fields.doc: Whether this is the message its thread is about; marks the card.

fields.name: foldable
fields.doc: How many replies sit under this one in the thread that built it. 0 hides the fold button.

fields.name: folded
fields.doc: Whether this reader folded those replies away.

fields.name: owned
fields.doc: Whether this message is a row inside a larger surface — a thread, a feed — rather than standing on its own. A row draws smaller. It keeps its own like / repost / fold either way.

components.name: Thread
components.doc: A conversation: the messages of a reply tree, flattened and indented by depth, each rendered as a Post of its own, with any subtree foldable.

messageDocs.name: folded
messageDocs.doc: A row folded its replies away — the thread is what knows which rows those are, so it drops them and stops the bubble here.

messageDocs.name: unfolded
messageDocs.doc: A row brought its replies back.

messageDocs.name: liked
messageDocs.doc: A row was liked. The thread keeps the flag for that row and hands the row back rebuilt, then lets the bubble travel on: only the component above can write to a PDS.

messageDocs.name: unliked
messageDocs.doc: A row's like was taken back.

messageDocs.name: reposted
messageDocs.doc: A row was reposted.

messageDocs.name: unreposted
messageDocs.doc: A row's repost was taken back.

messageDocs.name: summary
messageDocs.doc: How many messages there are, and how many are folded away.

fields.name: posts
fields.doc: The conversation in reading order, each message { uri, displayName, handle, text, createdAt, facets, images, replyCount, repostCount, likeCount, depth } — depth being how deep in the reply tree it sits.

fields.name: focus
fields.doc: The uri of the message the thread is about; that row is marked. Empty for none. Writing it rebuilds the rows.

inits.name: conversation
inits.argsJson: {"focus": "at://did:plc:alice000000000000000000/app.bsky.feed.post/3kaaa", "posts": [{"uri": "at://did:plc:alice000000000000000000/app.bsky.feed.post/3kaaa", "displayName": "Alice Alpha", "handle": "alice.bsky.social", "text": "shipped the thing: dynamic components that register into a running app at runtime", "createdAt": "2026-08-11T14:03:00Z", "replyCount": 2, "repostCount": 34, "likeCount": 1280, "depth": 0}, {"uri": "at://did:plc:bob00000000000000000000/app.bsky.feed.post/3kbbb", "displayName": "Bob Beta", "handle": "bob.bsky.social", "text": "does the host have to trust the bundle for this?", "createdAt": "2026-08-11T14:21:00Z", "replyCount": 1, "likeCount": 18, "depth": 1}, {"uri": "at://did:plc:alice000000000000000000/app.bsky.feed.post/3kccc", "displayName": "Alice Alpha", "handle": "alice.bsky.social", "text": "no — it declares a schema, and the views are data the host compiles. it never touches the DOM", "createdAt": "2026-08-11T14:40:00Z", "replyCount": 1, "likeCount": 44, "depth": 2}, {"uri": "at://did:plc:bob00000000000000000000/app.bsky.feed.post/3kddd", "displayName": "Bob Beta", "handle": "bob.bsky.social", "text": "that is the part I kept getting wrong. thanks!", "createdAt": "2026-08-11T15:02:00Z", "likeCount": 7, "depth": 3}, {"uri": "at://did:plc:carol0000000000000000000/app.bsky.feed.post/3keee", "displayName": "Carol Gamma", "handle": "carol.bsky.social", "text": "how big is one of these bundles?", "createdAt": "2026-08-11T15:30:00Z", "likeCount": 3, "depth": 1}]}
inits.doc: A five-message conversation three levels deep, focused on its root.

components.name: Profile
components.doc: One account: who it is, what it says about itself, its three counts, and its recent messages.

messageDocs.name: toggleFollow
messageDocs.doc: Follow this account, or unfollow it. Optimistic, and announced as a bubble.

messageDocs.name: followed
messageDocs.doc: This reader followed the account; carries its handle.

messageDocs.name: unfollowed
messageDocs.doc: This reader unfollowed the account; carries its handle.

messageDocs.name: summary
messageDocs.doc: The account and its counts, as one sentence.

messageDocs.name: followLabel
messageDocs.doc: What the follow button says right now.

messageDocs.name: liked
messageDocs.doc: A message in the feed was liked; the profile keeps the flag for that row, as a thread does.

messageDocs.name: unliked
messageDocs.doc: A message's like was taken back.

messageDocs.name: reposted
messageDocs.doc: A message in the feed was reposted.

messageDocs.name: unreposted
messageDocs.doc: A message's repost was taken back.

fields.name: displayName
fields.doc: The account's display name; the handle stands in when it is empty.

fields.name: handle
fields.doc: The account's handle, without the leading @.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: The account's own description of itself.

fields.name: followersCount
fields.doc: How many accounts follow it.

fields.name: followsCount
fields.doc: How many accounts it follows.

fields.name: postsCount
fields.doc: How many messages it has written.

fields.name: following
fields.doc: Whether this reader follows it, counted on top of followersCount.

fields.name: posts
fields.doc: Its recent messages, in the same shape a Thread's posts take; each becomes a Post of its own, standing on its own (no depth, nothing to fold).
